title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
metadata_mismatch: none (paper header dated November 5, 2026; arXiv v1 9 Nov 2026)
why_wsp: Provides an instruction set and transactional runtime for executing supplied weight-space intervention programs (ablate, project, rank-one) on pretrained LMs with scoped restoration; no LLM editor writes the programs in this paper (interventions are hand-specified or activation-derived).
editor: none (programs are supplied by the experimenter; directions measured from activations); companion NCP manuscript handles proposal generation
interface: code/tensor tools (shape-checked instruction set: ADD, SCALE, RANK1, PROJECT_OUT, WRITE_KEY, PRUNE)
loop: n/a (activation-based match-action rule selects a program per request; no editor iteration)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "Head ablation changed 36,864 entries. The MLP projection changed 884,666 of 884,736 entries after FP32 rounding." (Sec. 7.1, SmolLM); Qwen: "head edit changed 196,608 entries and the projection changed 13,753,919 entries" (Sec. 8.1)

headline_results.quote: hook versus materialized logits have maximum absolute difference 0.000183761 and RMS difference 0.000016225, with argmax agreement 1.0
all three modes produce the same token sequence at every measured length
Undo restored the original weights and recorded outputs; replay restored the edited state.

cost.quote: The four recorded combined-edit transactions took 9.2–14.6 ms, excluding inference.
W-ISA application medians are 48.866, 56.059 and 115.142 ms for the three length groups; restoration medians are 2.500, 2.413 and 2.624 ms

baselines_and_controls: Original unedited inference and an equivalent PyTorch forward hook; independent NumPy reference for stored projection; fresh-process replay.
runs_and_variance: Timing: "one warm-up and five timed repetitions" per mode/length, 45 timed requests; medians with IQR error bars (Fig. 1). Perplexity: single pass per condition.
robustness_of_edits: not tested (edits are request-scoped and restored by design)
verification: Byte-exact restoration check ("bytes(p_exit) = bytes(p_entry)"), parameter digests, NumPy reference matching with max abs diff 0.0; 66 software tests passed.
limitations_stated: No dedicated limitations section. Notes shared model lock serializes requests; snapshots cover full target tensors; materialized path pays snapshot/update/restore costs vs hook per-layer arithmetic.
code_or_data: none found (paper states MIT-licensed code but gives no URL)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog)
notes_for_survey: Infrastructure paper: an execution/transaction layer for weight interventions rather than an LLM-as-editor study. Relevant as tooling for safe, reversible, request-scoped WSP edits; the policy-proposal loop is deferred to a companion NCP manuscript.
